content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint may not capture foot-only response adequately",
      "quote": "Proportion of patients achieving an IGA (hand and foot) score of 0 or 1 at week 16",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint uses a single IGA score for hands and feet, but inclusion requires involvement of at least 2 anatomical areas (could be both hands, 1 hand and 1 foot, or both feet). A single score may not reflect differential response in hands vs feet, potentially diluting treatment effect if one area responds less.",
      "fix": "Consider separate IGA scores for hands and feet or a composite that requires improvement in both, or specify how the single score is derived when both areas are involved."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for emollient use is overly rigid and may cause screening failures",
      "quote": "At least 11 (of a total of 14*) applications of a topical emollient (moisturizer) during the 7 consecutive days immediately before the baseline visit (not including the day of randomization).",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "7.2.1",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring exactly 11 of 14 applications in the 7 days before baseline is a strict compliance threshold that may exclude otherwise eligible patients who miss a single application, leading to unnecessary screening failures and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Relax to a minimum number of applications (e.g., at least 10) or allow a grace period for missed applications."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for skin protection measures is vague and may be hard to verify",
      "quote": "Patients need to have been compliant with the skin protection measures (as outlined in Section 8.10.3) through the entire duration of the screening period (minimum of 4 weeks but lasting to a maximum of 8 weeks).",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "7.2.1",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The requirement for compliance with skin protection measures over a 4-8 week screening period is subjective and not objectively measurable, leading to potential inconsistencies in eligibility determination and likely amendments to clarify compliance assessment.",
      "fix": "Define specific, measurable compliance criteria (e.g., patient diary, counseling sessions) and document how compliance will be assessed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for patch test reactions may be overly broad and exclude relevant patients",
      "quote": "Patients with a positive patch test reaction to one or more allergens (a score of 1+ or above according to International Contact Dermatitis Research Group [ICDRG] grading scale) in either a. the baseline patch test series OR b. extended baseline or supplemental patch test allergens if such additional testing is conducted by the investigator OR c. Personal products if testing with such products is conducted by the investigator AND Which is deemed to be clinically relevant in the view of the investigator as the current cause of the hand and foot dermatitis.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "7.2.2",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The exclusion based on clinically relevant positive patch tests is subjective and may lead to inconsistent application across sites. Also, the note that patients with documented ACD are excluded regardless of current relevance is contradictory and may exclude patients who could benefit from dupilumab.",
      "fix": "Clarify the definition of 'clinically relevant' and consider excluding only those with current exposure to the allergen, not all with a history of ACD."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoint for HECSI is only for patients with hand dermatitis, but inclusion does not require hand involvement",
      "quote": "For patients with hand dermatitis, percent change from baseline to week 16 in Hand Eczema Severity Index (HECSI) score",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The inclusion criteria allow patients with only foot involvement (both feet) to be enrolled, but the HECSI secondary endpoints are only for patients with hand dermatitis. This creates a subset analysis that may not be powered, and the protocol does not specify how these patients will be identified or analyzed.",
      "fix": "Either require hand involvement for all patients or pre-specify a subgroup analysis for hand dermatitis patients with appropriate power considerations."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring lacks specific assessments for dupilumab-related conjunctivitis and eosinophilia",
      "quote": "Incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) through week 16",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.1.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Dupilumab is known to cause conjunctivitis and eosinophilia, but the safety endpoint is generic TEAEs without specific monitoring for these known adverse events. The protocol should include targeted assessments (e.g., ophthalmologic exams, eosinophil counts) to capture these events.",
      "fix": "Add specific safety monitoring for conjunctivitis (e.g., eye exams) and eosinophilia (e.g., lab tests) as part of the safety assessments."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for age is inconsistent with pediatric requirements for weight and consent",
      "quote": "Male or female ≥12 years old at time of the screening visit.",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "7.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The protocol includes adolescents (≥12 years) but does not specify weight requirements or pediatric-specific consent/assent procedures beyond a general statement. This may lead to amendments to address pediatric regulatory requirements.",
      "fix": "Add specific pediatric eligibility criteria (e.g., weight) and detailed assent/consent procedures for minors."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoint for EASI is only in patients with AD lesions elsewhere, but inclusion does not require this",
      "quote": "In patients with AD lesions on other parts of the body in addition to hands and feet; − Percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16",
      "page": 41,
      "section": "4.1.4",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The exploratory endpoint is only assessed in a subset of patients (those with AD lesions elsewhere), but the inclusion criteria do not require such lesions. This may lead to a small subset and limited power for exploratory analyses.",
      "fix": "Either require AD lesions elsewhere for all patients or pre-specify the subset and ensure adequate enrollment for this exploratory analysis."
    }
  ]
}
